calls.reason: Lovable reports Plinq reaching 10,000 users, while Pirxey describes a noncoder app needing engineering repairs. These mixed accounts do not settle Marcus's hedged expectation about dependable operation.
The February Cursor thread confirms Claude integration and some complaints, alongside favorable reactions. It does not establish a substantial group of deeply frustrated working programmers.

RCR and RSNA document shortages, and the Danish account describes doctors reassigned after task automation. None establishes the worldwide zero-displacement assertion, which Marcus also qualifies as his understanding.
HostingAdvice's February 2025 survey found 88% would encourage coding. A single baseline does not show whether AI enthusiasm subsequently increased discouragement directed at American children.

The forecast extends to at least 2035. MirrorCode's bounded reimplementations and the human design choices in Otto OS do not establish a decisive example of a big project succeeding without human architectural input.

CMU's driving history and Nature's analysis support persistent difficulty with rare failures. They do not establish that initial progress was easy or that this effort pattern occurs broadly across AI; the 80/20 framing remains a heuristic.
